subject: ps
fixes: c-ps-random-variables-expectation commonMistakes[1]: corrected the claim that the 'variance-of-a-sum and product rules need independence (or zero covariance)'. Zero covariance suffices for E[XY]=E[X]E[Y] and Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y), but Var(XY)=E[X^2]E[Y^2]-(E[X]E[Y])^2 needs independence; the text now states each assumption separately.

c-ps-covariance-correlation intuition: 'if X is symmetric about 0, Y=X^2 has zero correlation with X' was false when X^2 is constant (e.g. X=+/-1, where correlation is undefined) or E[X^4] is infinite; added the conditions E[X^4]<infinity and X^2 not constant.

c-ps-pmf-pdf-cdf math (Quantiles): 'More generally the p-quantile solves F(x_p)=p' implied a solution always exists (false for discrete X); now 'Under the same assumption' (continuous, strictly increasing F).
f-ps-normal meaning: added the missing condition a != 0 to aX+b ~ N(a*mu+b, a^2*sigma^2), matching the concept page.
f-ps-permutations variables: plain-text meaning showed a literal 'n_k' (the field is not Markdown-rendered); changed to the Unicode subscript form n1 + ... + nk = n.

c-ps-bayes-theorem gateRelevance: removed 'usually rounded to two or three decimal places' (unsupported: all three official DA Bayes NATs in the repo, 2024-Q58, 2025-Q31 and 2026-Q57, say two decimal places); now 'rounded as the question specifies'. Replaced 'The classic NAT/MCQ pattern' with 'A standard Bayes question', and the variants list with 'Variations to prepare for' (second-observation and further-observation variants have no official DA instance).

c-ps-hypothesis-tests gateRelevance: 'Typical question patterns' -> 'Question patterns to prepare for'; no official DA PYQ (2024-2026) is tagged ps-hypothesis-tests, so describing them as typical was unsupported.

c-ps-clt-confidence-intervals gateRelevance: 'Confidence-interval questions typically ask for' -> 'can ask for' (no official DA PYQ is tagged ps-confidence-interval); 'The CLT is examined through' -> 'can be examined through'.

c-ps-sample-space-axioms gateRelevance: 'Typically examined through short MCQ/NAT computations' -> 'Questions can be short MCQ/NAT computations'; 'MSQs test ... range questions ask for' -> 'can test ... can ask for' (no official instance of an axiom MSQ or a P(A and B) range question).

c-ps-conditional-joint-marginal gateRelevance: 'It is examined directly ... Typical patterns: joint PMF tables, sometimes with an unknown constant' -> 'It can be examined directly ... is needed inside ... Patterns to prepare for: ... possibly with an unknown constant' (several listed patterns have no official instance).

Frequency wording removed from the remaining gateRelevance fields (no frequency claim is supported by content/exam/pattern.json): c-ps-counting ('is examined' -> 'can be examined', 'Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for'); c-ps-independent-vs-mutually-exclusive, c-ps-covariance-correlation and c-ps-conditional-expectation ('Examined as' -> 'Can be examined as'); c-ps-central-tendency-dispersion ('Typically examined as' -> 'Questions can be'); c-ps-random-variables-expectation ('Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for', '(often NAT)' -> '(NAT or MCQ)'); c-ps-pmf-pdf-cdf ('Often examined through the CDF' -> 'Questions can be posed through the CDF', 'MSQs test' -> 'MSQs can test'); c-ps-bernoulli-binomial-uniform and c-ps-normal-t-chi-squared ('Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for'); c-ps-joint-conditional-pdf ('Typically examined ... (often on a triangular region)' -> 'Can be examined ... (for example on a triangular region)'); c-ps-uniform-exponential-poisson ('Typically examined' -> 'Can be examined', 'Typical patterns' -> 'Patterns to prepare for', '(often inside ...)' -> '(for example inside ...)').
